core_obligations: Assume the first condition and compute Ext groups from the bounded complex of injectives, obtaining the vanishing for all modules and hence the second condition (proof lines 17542-17555).
Note that the second condition implies the third immediately (proof lines 17555-17558).
Assume the third condition and use the exactness of Hom from the ring to show the cohomology of K vanishes outside the interval (proof lines 17558-17566).

Choose a right resolution of K by injectives concentrated in the interval, replace the top term by the kernel and conclude through a distinguished triangle that K has injective amplitude in the interval (proof lines 17566-17586).
proof_roadmap: (1) implies (2) by computing Ext from injectives (proof lines 17542-17555).
(3) gives the vanishing of cohomology outside the interval (proof lines 17558-17566).
Resolve by injectives and use a distinguished triangle to finish (proof lines 17566-17586).
difficulty_reason: The lemma characterises a complex of bounded injective amplitude in three ways, the third testing only against quotients of the ring by ideals, and the proof is a 45-line argument that walks around the equivalence. From a bounded complex of injectives it computes the Ext groups by the Hom complex into the injectives, which gives the vanishing for all modules; the implication to the bounded-test version is immediate; and the converse is the substantial part, where vanishing against quotients is used to show first that the cohomology is concentrated in the interval, then that the complex admits a right resolution by injectives vanishing below the interval, and finally that the truncation at the upper end can be replaced by an injective through a distinguished triangle. The construction of the resolution and the triangle step are the content, and both are displayed.
